processes.name: Process
look.designError: Could not switch the design. Restart the app and try again.
look.designNote: Shared by all widgets. GPT Design applies as each widget becomes ready; view, size and state are preserved.
look.designScope: Metric colours are shared. Glass and background colour bases apply to Claude Design.
look.language.title: Language
app.unknownWidget: Widget “{id}” is not in the registry.
source.sidecarMissing: Sidecar not found — build it: npm run sidecar
source.sidecarGarbled: Could not read the sidecar reply: {error}
source.sidecarSilent: Sidecar did not answer within {seconds} s
spotify.error.noDevice: no active device — open Spotify and play something
spotify.error.restricted: Spotify did not allow this action
spotify.error.wait: Spotify asks you to wait {seconds} s
spotify.error.playerGarbled: could not read the player reply: {error}
spotify.error.timeout: Spotify did not answer in time
spotify.error.portsBusy: all callback ports are in use ({ports}). Free one and try again
spotify.error.loginTimeout: no reply from the sign-in page
spotify.error.needsAuth: the Spotify connection is no longer valid
spotify.error.noRandom: the system could not provide randomness: {error}
spotify.page.doneNote: You can close this tab — the widget is connecting.
spotify.page.mismatchNote: This looks like an old sign-in tab.
totp.error.dirtyTail: the secret has trailing bits — the entry is damaged
totp.error.noName: the entry needs a name: issuer or label
totp.error.nothing: nothing to add: the line is empty
totp.error.notOtpauth: this is not an otpauth:// link
totp.error.hotp: this is a counter-based code (hotp), but the widget shows time-based codes
mail.error.badMailbox: the mailbox link must be a plain http or https address
speedtest.error.noBytes: Server did not report the byte count
output.error.cannotWrite: Cannot write to the output folder
license.own: © 2026 CommonFool. MIT License: you may freely use, modify and distribute the app, provided the copyright notice and the licence text are kept. Provided “as is”, without warranty of any kind.
license.bundledNote: Licences: {list}. All of this code is used unmodified. Authors, links to the source code and the full licence texts are in the full list.
license.about.programs: Not included in the app: downloaded only when you press the button, from the authors’ official releases, and run as separate programs under their own licences.
license.note.openmeteo: Weather data by Open-Meteo.com, licensed under CC BY 4.0.
license.note.mlab: M-Lab publishes speed test results, including your IP address, date and time, as open data.
license.note.spotify: Spotify is a trademark of Spotify AB. This app is not affiliated with or endorsed by Spotify.
license.fullHint: Opens THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt: every component with its version, licence and the full licence texts.
support.thanks: Thank you for using Windgets! The app is free and open source. If you find it useful, you can support its development.
reminder.title: Enjoying Windgets?
reminder.text: The app is free and has no ads. If it has been useful to you, consider supporting its development.
support.about.monobank: Monobank jar: pay by card from any bank.
support.about.kofi: One-off donation by card or PayPal.
support.about.crypto: Any currency you like: BTC, ETH, USDT, USDC, SOL, TON and more.
support.scan: Or point your phone camera at the code.
settings.widgets.allHidden: All widgets are hidden by “Hide all widgets” in the “Behaviour” section. While it is on, no widget windows are shown.
settings.widgets.throughAll: All widgets let the mouse through
settings.widgets.clickable: This widget takes clicks, so it needs the mouse
settings.widgets.noGpu: No discrete graphics card — nothing to show
settings.widgets.columnsNote: Columns: enable the module — a disabled one is not loaded at all, no window and no background work; keep it above others; let clicks pass through; lock it in place. A dash means the widget takes clicks and needs the mouse.
settings.widgets.locksOverridden: Locks are overridden by “Lock positions” in the “Behaviour” section: while it is on, every window is locked. The per-widget checkmarks are kept and come back when it is turned off.
settings.windows.snappingHint: A window snaps within eight pixels of an edge and lets go at ten.
settings.windows.lockHint: Widgets cannot be moved or resized. This window still can.
settings.windows.hideHint: Widgets are hidden, but the list of enabled ones is kept: turn this off and the same ones come back.
settings.windows.autostartHint: A Task Scheduler task with administrator rights — for the installed version.
settings.windows.resetNote: Lays the open windows out in a grid on the main monitor and restores their default sizes. Rescues a window lost off-screen.
settings.source.idle: Sensors are not polled: hardware modules are off
settings.source.note: Hardware is read by the built-in sidecar — there is no need to run LibreHardwareMonitor. Administrator rights are required: without them, drives, the motherboard and the CPU temperature cannot be read.
settings.source.stepNote: Chart history is counted in samples: at a two-second interval the columns stretch from five minutes to ten.
settings.source.folderNote: Spotify credentials and the speed test history are kept there too.
settings.source.logNote: The app writes failures and errors here. Attach the file to a bug report — it is never sent anywhere on its own.
theme.classic: CPU amber, GPU cyan, memory blue, media green.
theme.polar: Three blues for the system. Green sets upload apart.
theme.indigo: Blue, ice and indigo. Pink for upload.
theme.mint: Three mints, calm borders and coral upload.
theme.spectrum: Amber CPU, cyan GPU, lilac memory and green media.
theme.a: Cool system, green activity and amber memory.
theme.b: Blue UI, lilac GPU and media, pink memory and upload.
theme.c: Cyan CPU, amber GPU and media, crimson memory.
look.mode.monochrome: White and distinct shades of grey
look.accentColorUsage: Buttons and graphics card. Other data is in shades of grey.
look.whiteText: Regular text and lowercase password letters stay white.
look.vividNote: At 100 % the theme colours are unchanged. The slider changes colour brightness in every window; the background and regular text keep their colour.
look.opacityNote: Applies to widgets. The settings window is always opaque.
look.scaleNote: Resizes widgets together with text and spacing. A widget’s own scale is under the gear in the list.
look.paletteNote: Colours and controls are shared by the selected design. GPT and Claude remember their palette and custom colours separately.
look.legendTheme: The palette colours controls, metrics and states; weather and password character types use the same roles.
look.legendNeutral: Data and states are neutral; controls follow the mode’s accent. Values, labels and icons distinguish metrics.
look.legendBases: Four colours repeat in the same roles.
look.legendWhite: Regular text and lowercase password letters are white.
look.glassNote: Surface tint works in both designs. GPT and Claude remember their glass separately; opacity is independent.
page.notFound: Widget not found: this version doesn't have it.
page.coverNote: The cover does not change the window size: the card adapts to it.
page.sizeFlexible: The window is resized with the mouse: as many rows as fit are shown.
page.sizeNote: Each size is named after what disappears from the card. There are no sizes in between: between two steps the card just gets narrower.
page.opacityHint: The widget follows the shared slider in “Appearance”. Move this slider and it gets its own opacity.
page.scaleHint: The widget follows the shared slider in “Appearance”. Move this slider and it gets its own scale, and the window follows.
mail.settings.imapNote: Connects over IMAP, secured with SSL/TLS.
mail.settings.passwordNote: It must be an app password, not your mail password: Gmail, for example, does not accept the regular password over IMAP at all.
mail.settings.mailboxNote: Where the “Open mailbox” button leads. If left empty, the address is derived from the server name and shown in the field as a hint. Your own value overrides it; clear the field to get the suggested address back.
mail.settings.previewNote: The start of the message as a third line under the subject. Polling then fetches 64 KB of each of the ten messages; when off, message bodies are not requested.
totp.settings.inputNote: Paste the whole link from under the QR code — the issuer and label come from it. The secret can also be typed by hand: spaces, dashes and case do not matter.
totp.settings.label: Label
totp.settings.namesNote: With a pasted link both fields are filled from it; by hand they are only needed for a secret typed on its own.
totp.settings.none: None yet. Codes appear in the card right after the first one.
totp.settings.entriesHint: The card uses this same order; drag an entry by its left edge to change it. Codes are computed from the Windows clock: if a service rejects them, check the time and time zone.
totp.settings.dpapiNote: Secrets are encrypted with your Windows account’s key and become unreadable after reinstalling Windows. Keep the codes on your phone too, or save the recovery codes.
spotify.settings.note: Sound comes from the Spotify desktop app or web player; the widget controls them. Premium is required.
spotify.settings.disconnectNote: Erases the saved token. The Client ID stays, so signing in again takes one click.
spotify.settings.clientIdHint: Client ID from the Spotify Developer Dashboard
spotify.settings.noSecret: No client secret is needed: that is what PKCE is for.
spotify.settings.urisNote: The first is the main one; the others are used if its port is busy.
weather.settings.removeNote: Without a city the weather widget does not go online at all.
weather.settings.sourceNote: Weather comes from Open-Meteo — no key and no account. It is fetched every four hours and only while the widget is visible.
media.settings.none: None yet. A source appears here by itself as soon as something plays.
media.settings.sourcesHint: A source appears by itself when an app first plays something; unchecking hides it from the card. Windows reports only the app, not the website: the whole browser is one source.
downloader.settings.note: yt-dlp checks for updates by itself once a day and updates at once when a site breaks. QuickJS solves YouTube’s JavaScript challenges for it; FFmpeg merges video with audio and makes MP3.
tools.failure.noBuild: Download not found — update the app
tools.failure.noChecksum: GitHub gave no checksum — not installed
tools.failure.rateLimited: GitHub limit reached — try again in an hour
tools.failure.inUse: In use — a conversion or download is running
tools.gate.source: From the official releases on GitHub, verified with SHA-256
tools.noDesktop: Desktop not found — pick a folder yourself
tools.folderNote: Results never overwrite existing files: a taken name gets “ (1)”, “ (2)”. If your desktop syncs with OneDrive, large videos go to the cloud too.
tools.note: The app downloads these programs itself, only on request: from the authors’ official releases on GitHub, verified by SHA-256. FFmpeg already installed on the system is used as is.
tools.system: from the system — updated by whoever installed it
clipboard.clearHint: Forget the list and empty the clipboard itself
notes.erase: Erase this note — you can bring it back
media.idleHint: Start music or a video anywhere
media.moreSources_one: {count} more source playing — click to switch
media.moreSources_other: {count} more sources playing — click to switch
hardware.drivesHidden: All drives are hidden — pick them in the widget settings
hardware.noGpu: No discrete graphics card, only integrated graphics. You can turn this widget off in settings
disks.settings.title: Show on the card
disks.settings.hint: Which drives to show. A new drive appears on the card by itself, and the window takes the height of the drives shown.
disks.settings.waiting: The drive list appears once the widget is on and the sensors answer.
disks.settings.last: The last drive shown can't be hidden: to hide the whole card, clear “On” in the Widgets section.
metrics.title: Show on the card
metrics.hint: An unchecked row leaves the card, and the window gets shorter. Load always stays.
metrics.boardHint: Which board sensor to show. “Automatic” goes by the name the board gives; on an unfamiliar board the fans are called “Fan #1…”, and you can pick the right one here by its live reading.
metrics.waiting: The list appears once the widget is on and the sensors answer.
weather.place.offlineNote: Without a city the widget stays offline
spotify.setup.lead: Paste the app’s Client ID from the Spotify Developer Dashboard. No client secret is needed.
spotify.idleHint: Play something in Spotify — the widget will pick it up
spotify.nowhere: Spotify is not running or was not found.
spotify.nowhereAsk: Open the app or the web player?
spotify.authorizing: The sign-in page is open in your browser — finish there.
mail.noAccountHint: Set it up in widget settings
mail.error.gone: this mailbox no longer exists — it was removed
mail.settings.boxesHint: Each mailbox gets its own tab on the card, plus one more, “All”, where letters from every mailbox share one list. Click a row to open the mailbox.
mail.check.incomplete: enter the server and the login
mail.error.noDecrypt: could not decrypt the saved password: {error}
mail.check.passed: Letters in Inbox: {messages}, unread: {unseen}. Answered in {seconds} s.
mail.check.timeout: The server has been silent for over 15 seconds — step “{step}”
mail.check.title.greeting: The server didn't answer as IMAP
mail.check.title.inbox: Signed in, but Inbox didn't open
mail.check.hint.resolve: {host} isn't in DNS: check the IMAP server address — for example, imap.gmail.com.
mail.check.hint.connect: Can't connect to {host}:{port}: check the port (usually 993), the network and any VPN.
mail.check.hint.tls: Port {port} isn't encrypted or the certificate was rejected: IMAP over TLS usually uses 993, not 143.
mail.check.hint.greeting: Something other than IMAP answers at {host}:{port}: make sure it's the incoming mail server, not SMTP or webmail.
mail.check.hint.login: The login or password didn't fit. Gmail, Outlook and many others need an app password, not the regular one.
mail.check.hint.inbox: The server let you in but refused the INBOX folder — its answer is below.
mail.error.tooMany: there are already {limit} mailboxes — no room for another
mail.signInHint: Check the account in widget settings
converter.mixed: Mixed file types — convert them separately
converter.listen: Listen from the start of the cut
downloader.reason.broken: The site changed and yt-dlp can’t read it yet
downloader.badUrl: Paste a link that starts with http
clipboard.clearFailed: Could not clear the clipboard. Try again.
converter.nextRunOptions: Changes apply to the next run
downloader.dismissFailure: Dismiss error and return to the URL
theme.gpt: Original GPT palette: green controls, orange CPU, turquoise GPU and blue memory.
pawnio.title: PawnIO driver
pawnio.gate.why: Without it the CPU and motherboard report no temperature, clock, power or fans
pawnio.gate.restartWhy: The PawnIO driver is installed and will work after a restart
pawnio.source: Open-source signed driver by namazso · {size} from GitHub, SHA-256 verified
pawnio.note: A kernel driver LibreHardwareMonitor uses to read the CPU and the motherboard chip: temperature, clock, power, voltage and fans. The GPU, memory, network and drives don't need it. It is installed only when you click: Windgets downloads the author's official installer from GitHub, verifies its SHA-256 and runs it.
pawnio.notOurs: Not installed by Windgets — remove it where it was installed from
pawnio.stays: Uninstalling Windgets leaves the driver in place: other programs may use it too
update.title: Updates
update.note: The installer is downloaded from GitHub, verified by checksum and installed over this version. Windows will close and reopen in the new version; settings are kept.
update.autoHint: Ask GitHub once a week whether a new version is out. Updates are downloaded and installed only when you click.
update.stage.installing: Installer started — the app will close now
update.failure.noBuild: The release has no installer yet — try again later
update.failure.dev: Updates aren't installed in a development build
